## Where the documentation is

- For this repo: `../snowy-docs/repos/snowy-wp/`

No documentation lives in here. If you are going to write some, it goes there.

## How we work here

**For any development task, the cycle is `flow`**: understand, isolate the
space, plan, develop, pass the gate, propose and close. That skill explains the
order and why that order.

The steps, if you need to go straight to one:

| Moment | What to invoke |
| ------ | -------------- |
| You arrive and do not know the repo | `repo-map` |
| You are about to start working | `workspace` — your branch and your environment, without stepping on anyone |
| Before touching code | `explain-plan` |
| Something fails and you do not know why | `root-cause` |
| You are about to commit | `ship` |
| You have finished | `workspace finish` — pushes the branch and opens the proposal |
| You close the session | `end-session` |

## Non-negotiable rules

- **Before the first file of a task, open the project's conventions.** They are
  written; the failure is not that they are missing, it is reading them after
  writing the code, when they only serve to reorder it. Gate 4 of `/ship` puts
  them in front of you again, but by then it is already rework.
- **If you change code that invalidates a doc, you update it in the same turn.**
- **Project notes and references go to git**, not to local memory.
- Conventional commits, body lines of 100 characters, no `Co-Authored-By` and no
  emojis. A change proposal's description does not carry the tool's signature or
  a "generated with" line either.
- No comments that narrate what the code already says.
